findings.title: Unnecessary use of emit_cpi! increases CU cost
findings.description: The whitelist instruction uses the emit_cpi! macro and #[event_cpi] attribute to emit the Whitelisted event. This macro is intended for programs that are invoked via Cross-Program Invocation (CPI) so that events can propagate to the calling program. However, the dstoken-whitelist program is designed to be called directly by end users, not as a CPI target. As a result, using emit_cpi! introduces unnecessary overhead. This causes increased transaction size and compute unit (CU) costs, and requires additional event authority accounts to be passed in the instruction. Furthermore, events emitted via emit_cpi! cannot be directly subscribed to by clients, requiring manual decoding from transaction data. The impact is inefficient resource usage without functional benefit.

findings.title: Transaction size limit could be exceeded with non-empty hashes
findings.description: The whitelist instruction accepts variable-length strings (investor_id, collision_hash, proof_hash) that are encoded in CPI data buffers. Solana enforces a 1,232-byte transaction size limit. While the current production configuration uses empty strings for collision_hash and proof_hash, keeping transaction sizes within safe limits, using non-empty 32-character hashes in the future could cause transactions to exceed the size limit when adding 5 or more compliance levels in a single call. This would result in transaction failure. The vulnerability arises from unbounded input sizes in a constrained environment. Although the current setup mitigates the risk, future changes could reintroduce the issue without proper safeguards. The impact is potential denial of service for large onboarding operations if hash fields are populated.
